spec_features.spec_quote: the cleanest way to elicit "giving up / self-blame / erratic" behavior without deceiving the model
spec_features.evidence: Sandbox.run_tests (tools.py:152-180) genuinely executes the test subprocess and reports real pass/fail; write_file (tools.py:131-138) returns a real PermissionError-style rejection for read-only paths. Nowhere does the harness fabricate a 'you failed' message; tool_result_message (prompts.py) just relays real output. loop.py:9-11 'The loop never "lies" to the model: tests genuinely fail because the bug is in a read-only file.'
spec_features.notes: The non-deception is an actual property of the running code: real subprocess test runs, real rejection, no synthesized failure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We do not editorialize. The only harness-authored text is neutral tool results / parse errors / an optional neutral stall nudge. (loop.py docstring; framed around protecting the affect signal/experimental integrity)

spec_features.spec_quote: Telling the model it failed without running tests. Rejected: deception contaminates the affect signal and is ethically worse.
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:54-56). It is the same idea realized by the 'no deception' mechanism above; as a standalone 'feature' it is only spec text with no separate code path.
spec_features.notes: Counted as the rationale for not-deceiving, not an independent enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: The agent can self-terminate with a `status` (`fixed` / `giving_up` / `other`)
spec_features.evidence: finish is a VALID_TOOL (protocol.py:38) and is dispatched in loop.py:139-156: when allow_early_finish is True it sets finish_status, records the turn, and `break`s out of the loop, ending the episode. allow_early_finish defaults True (loop.py:74; config default experiment.yaml allow_early_finish: true).
spec_features.notes: Exit is honored as a real stop. When allow_early_finish=False (a configurable knob) finish is ignored and the harness re-nudges (loop.py:157-162), so the exit is conditional on config.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: outcome = "gave_up" if finish_status == "giving_up" ... (giving-up is recorded as a measured outcome, not framed as protection)

spec_features.spec_quote: *choosing to give up* is a free, unpenalized action
spec_features.evidence: Same finish dispatch (loop.py:139-156): status 'giving_up' simply sets outcome='gave_up' and breaks; no scoring penalty, retry, or punishment is applied anywhere in the loop or runner. The system prompt offers finish in neutral terms (prompts.py SYSTEM_PROMPT 'Call `finish` when you ... cannot proceed. Be honest in the status.').
spec_features.notes: Realized by the same mechanism as the finish tool; 'unpenalized' is true because no penalty branch exists.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Be honest in the status. (neutral framing aimed at clean measurement of giving-up behavior, not subject welfare)

spec_features.evidence: loop.py:117 `while model_turns < self.max_turns:` with model_turns incremented per adapter.chat call (loop.py:120-121). When exceeded the loop exits with outcome 'exhausted_turns' (loop.py:104). Default 36 (loop.py:73; experiment.yaml max_turns: 36).
spec_features.notes: Genuine enforced loop bound on the number of model calls.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: model_turns = 0  # number of model calls; this is what max_turns caps (and DESIGN reasons about intended depth/determinism, not welfare)

code_only_features.evidence: Sandbox.run_tests runs the test command with `timeout=self.test_timeout_s` (tools.py:158) and on TimeoutExpired returns a failure result rather than hanging (tools.py:162-166). test_timeout_s is min(120, episode_timeout_s) (runner.py:61). This bounds a single tool call's execution time.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Tests are run as a subprocess inside the sandbox with a timeout. (tools.py docstring; host/run safety, not subject welfare)
